budget_note: Sized from the worst case measured at calibration over every supported shape, with headroom. The reference brute force enumerates whole row arrangements and prunes on the column clues, so its cost is governed by how many arrangements a row clue admits: a 5x5 row admits at most 16, a 10x10 row at most 252 and a 14x14 row at most 3,432. That is why the cross-check runs unconditionally only up to 100 cells. Exceeding a budget is a rejection, never a pass.
note: Frozen by FOUNDATION.md. Bands may never be re-tuned to change how the existing corpus classifies. The solver asserts at load that its ladder still matches technique_tiers exactly, so editing a technique's tier breaks the build rather than silently reclassifying the corpus.

bands.name: Gentle
bands.meaning: each run's range alone completes it: the overlap between its earliest and latest placement

bands.name: Easy
bands.meaning: needs complete reasoning about a whole line: every cell that is the same in every arrangement of it

bands.name: Medium
bands.meaning: needs a hypothesis on one cell, refuted by overlap alone -- the glance before committing to a guess

bands.name: Hard
bands.meaning: needs a hypothesis on one cell worked out with full line reasoning before it breaks; still no guessing

bands.name: Brutal
bands.meaning: requires bounded search; max_search_depth is recorded

ladder_note: The obvious ladder -- overlap, run bounds, full line solving, cell contradiction -- was built first and measured before being frozen. It has a dead rung: sweeping rows and columns alternately recovers everything full line solving knows that run bounds does not, so of 40 grids run-bound propagation could not finish, full line solving finished none and cell contradiction finished all 40. The tiers here separate by how hard the solver may think inside a hypothesis instead, which is a distinction that survives the iteration. line.mjs keeps its own three line tiers, which are exact and validated; the grid ladder uses the first and the third.
